liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Drums** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer praises the drums/space segment as a prime example of Bill and Mickey's drumming genius; A P.A. outage seems to occur for about 90 seconds during Drums [4][14]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): The band shook off early rustiness during Sugaree, leading to a solid first set [8]
- **Loser** (1 review): Reviewer notes no mixing board or pedal board activity on Loser, wondering whether power failed [12]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Scarlet has a distinctly Caribbean feel that suits the venue [8]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-11-25.sbd.miller.112817.flac24** (recommended): soundboard; 15 songs; 120 min; rated 4.12/5 by 8 [1]. Said about its sound: This transfer has better stereo separation and overall sound than the earlier version, with the intro restored and no break in Drums [16]
- **gd1982-11-25.sbd.fried-lai.speed-corrected-fixed.jterrapin.126243.flac16**: soundboard; 15 songs; 113 min [3]
- **gd1982-11-25.134119.nak300.schley.flac1644**: audience recording; 13 songs; 91 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]. Said about its sound: Let It Grow cuts out, Fire is partly missing, and Good Lovin' cuts just before the end; a left-channel dropout was covered [4]
- **gd1982-11-25.sbd.miller.112816.flac16**: soundboard; 15 songs; 120 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [2]

## Around the show

- As the sun rose over the hills, a rainbow appeared to the right of the stage during the set [7]
- First set was professionally filmed with several cameras; the footage has not circulated, and crews seemingly left afterward [13]
- First set began around 4:45 am; Phil tuning drew Rastas shouting, and he asked if they'd never seen a sunrise [13]
- Attendee describes the show as tight, well played and spunky, though nothing unusual happened [17]
- Reviewer says Deadbase panned this show, but considers it average rather than bad [7]
- Reviewer rates it below a Top 10 show but more enjoyable than most late-80s and 90s shows [8]
- Reviewer had only seen this show under the 11/26/82 date; five copies are wrongly listed as 11/25 [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-11-25.sbd.miller.112817.flac24**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90/Dolby B) [1]
- **gd1982-11-25.sbd.fried-lai.speed-corrected-fixed.jterrapin.126243.flac16**: transferred by jterrapin; source: SDB>>MR>>PCM>>DAT>>CDR>>SHN>>TLH>>FLAC8; tech notes: shorten files recoded to flac8 w/traders little helper v2.7.0 the source(B. Fried's) ran about 4 cents too… [3]. Also: Source from B. Fried ran about four cents fast; corrected by -4.200% in Audacity and exported as FLAC [3]
- **gd1982-11-25.134119.nak300.schley.flac1644**: taped by Brian Schley; transferred by Andrew F.; source: AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX Metal. Set up FOB, recording by Brian Schley. [4]. Also: First lossless audience recording to circulate as of August 2015; the tape is incomplete [4]
- **gd1982-11-25.sbd.miller.112816.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90/Dolby B) [2]
